styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Tiles, fado houses and miradouro views over the river.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Custard tarts, grilled sardines and cheap tascas.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Age of Discovery monuments in Belém and the old Moorish hill.

stays.why: Flat, central grid near the river, tram 15 and metro. Easiest base for first-timers and walking.
Oldest quarter, steep lanes and fado bars. Charming but hilly and noisy at night.
Upscale shopping and cafés, walkable to Baixa and Bairro Alto. Good mix of comfort and location.
Nightlife heart; quiet by day, loud on weekend nights. Close to Chiado and Príncipe Real.

food: Try a pastel de nata warm with cinnamon; the famous Belém bakery queues are long, many cafés are just as good.
Eat grilled sardines and bacalhau (salt cod) in a simple tasca; lunch menus often cost €8–15.
Order a bifana (pork sandwich) or a prego for a cheap snack, about €3–6.
Seafood is best near the river and in Cascais; check the price per kilo before ordering.
Vegetarian and vegan options are growing in Chiado and Príncipe Real; check menus on the day.
more_time: Swap a city day for Sintra: train from Rossio, about 40 minutes, to palaces and gardens. Go early, it gets crowded.
Take a half-day trip to Cascais or Belém by train along the river for beaches and the tower.
Spend an evening in a fado house in Alfama or Mouraria; book ahead and expect a cover charge.

recommend.why: Three nights covers Baixa, Alfama, Belém and a fado night without rushing; add a day for Sintra.

month_notes: Jan: cool and wet, highs near 15°C. Pack a rain jacket and warm layers.
Feb: still cool, about 16°C, with some rain. Fewer crowds at the sights.
Mar: mild at 17°C but one of the wetter months; bring an umbrella.
Apr: warming to 19°C, rain still possible. Good for walking the hills.
May: pleasant at 23°C and drier. A great month for sightseeing.
Jun: warm and mostly dry, around 25°C. Long evenings and festival season starts.
Jul: hot and very dry, highs near 28°C. Go early or late; shade is scarce.
Aug: hottest and driest, about 28°C. Crowded; book restaurants and fado ahead.
Sep: still warm at 26°C with a little rain returning. Quieter than August.
Oct: mild at 23°C but rain days rise. Carry a light rain layer.
Nov: cooler at 18°C and wetter; good for museums and food.
Dec: cool at 16°C with rain; festive lights in Baixa and Chiado.

climate_guide.summary: Mild Atlantic climate: warm dry summers, cool wet winters, and rain mostly from October to March.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Warm and mostly dry, highs 23–28°C. Ideal for walking, trams and the riverfront.

items.title: Wettest: October to March
items.text: Around 8–10 rain days a month. Showers pass; pack a compact umbrella.

items.title: July and August are hot
items.text: Highs near 28°C and very dry. Sightsee early morning and rest in the afternoon.

items.title: Atlantic breeze
items.text: The river and ocean keep evenings cooler; a light layer helps after sunset.

items.title: Rain is rarely all day
items.text: Winter rain comes in spells. Plan indoor sights like museums as backup.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable shoes for cobbled hills, sunscreen and a hat in summer, a rain jacket in winter.

transit.best: Metro and walking for the centre; trams for the scenic hills.

modes.text: Fast and cheap. The red line links the airport to the centre with one change.
Carris buses cover the city. Buy a rechargeable Navegante card for about €0.50.
Trams 15 and 28 are scenic but crowded; watch for pickpockets.
Taxis use meters; insist on the meter and keep a receipt. Uber, Bolt and FreeNow work; look for the TVDE sign.
Driving in the centre is slow and parking is hard. Skip it for city days.
Walking works well on the flat Baixa; expect steep hills in Alfama and Bairro Alto.
